newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: CRICKET-BANGLADESH GOES CRAZY AFTER WIN VS SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BANGLADESH GOES CRAZY AFTER WIN VS SCOTLAND.

text.p: Cricket-crazy Bangladeshis walked off the job on Wednesday to join noisy nationwide victory marches after the country's semi-final win over Scotland in the ICC trophy tournament in Malaysia.
The 72-run victory means Bangladesh qualify for a place in the 1999 cricket World Cup in England, the first time they have achieved such heights.
"It's the biggest celebration since independence in 1971," said a journalist in the southern town of Khulna.
Shouting students left class waving national flags to join the street celebrations while government officials and office staff left work chanting "Victory for the Tigers".
Thousands of people joined marches in Dhaka and other main cities, witnesses said, amid exploding firecrackers, band music and paint being hurled in all directions.
In Chittagong, home of Bangladesh captain Akram Khan, hundreds of firecrackers exploded as state-run radio reported the last Scottish wicket to fall.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday pledged a car for all the players if Bangladesh qualified for the World Cup.
Telecommunications Minister Mohammad Nasim has pledged a mobile telephone each and Health Minister Salauddin Yusuf has offered free life-long medicare for the players.
Bangladesh face Kenya in the International Cricket Council final on Saturday.
When Bangladesh failed to qualify for last year's World Cup, hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka, angry protesters took to the street overturning and burning cars.
